answer: Require each identity to answer a fresh cipher puzzle inside a tight live round-trip window, measured from rotating probes scattered like a nebula: the puzzle is issued per identity, per epoch, and must be solved in one sequential exchange, so a single operator proxying many fakes through one box cannot answer them all in time, while quartz clocks on each probe timestamp the exchange and identities whose delays correlate get grouped as one farm and discounted. Running a thousand fakes then needs a thousand distinct, low-latency network vantages, not just cheap compute.
